transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

They told me I had to come see you because... well, they say my talking gets all mixed up. Like, I'll just be trying to explain about the keys. I have this heavy ring of keys for the night shift, cleaning the offices, you know? And the metal clinking, it always makes me think about the jail. Which is funny because I was just telling my supervisor about the jail, and then the prayer rug. You ever see a real woven prayer rug? The patterns on them are exactly like how chess pieces move. The knights, specifically, they do that L-shape jump. I used to carve chess pieces out of soap a long time ago, back before I dropped out of school. 

But anyway, I try to explain all this to people—the keys, the jail, the rug, the chess pieces—and they just look at me blank. They tell me they cannot follow what I am saying at all. So I guess that's what brings me here.
Have you been feeling unusually high or euphoric lately?

High? Yeah, I guess you could say that. There are days, you know, where I just feel... powerful. Like I'm vibrating with it. I'll be laughing, talking loud to everyone in the building, just feeling on top of the world. But then, you know, if someone looks at me wrong or questions what I'm doing, I just snap. I'll start shouting over the littlest things. Like the other day, this guy asked me why I was using the blue mop bucket instead of the yellow one. The blue one, it’s got these wheels that squeak, and the squeak sounds exactly like a mouse I used to have when I was a kid. A white mouse with red eyes. I kept him in a glass tank, and he'd run on that wheel all night. Squeak, squeak, squeak. My mom hated it. She said it kept her up, but she was always up anyway, smoking cigarettes in the kitchen. She smoked those long ones, the 100s. The smoke would just hang there in the air, like a ghost. I always thought smoke looked like ghosts trying to form a shape, you know? But yeah, the bucket... I just yelled at him. Over a bucket.
Have you ever heard voices when no one else was there?

Voices? Yeah, I do. Sometimes when I'm working, I'll hear this man's voice. It comes right out of the air vents, or sometimes when I'm alone in the mop closet. He says my name, or he tells me that I ruined everything. And it's not like a thought, it sounds exactly like someone is standing right next to my ear. Which is crazy because the mop closet is so small, you know? It's barely big enough for the buckets and the industrial floor wax. That floor wax smells terrible, by the way. It smells like old lemons and chemicals. Reminds me of the time I tried to fix up this old Chevy Nova I had. I bought it off a guy who lived two towns over. He had this huge dog, a Mastiff, I think. Thing weighed more than I did. It just sat on the porch the whole time we were doing the paperwork. I never did get that car running right. The carburetor was completely shot. You need a good carburetor if you're gonna go anywhere, otherwise the engine just floods. But yeah, the voice in the closet... it's just as real as you talking to me right now.
Have you heard that voice during times when you were not feeling especially high or powerful?

Yeah, I still hear him then, too. Like, there was a stretch... maybe a month ago? I wasn't feeling all wired up and powerful, and I wasn't feeling totally dragged down either. Just sort of regular, you know? Just doing my shift. But even then, for like two or three weeks straight, I still heard the man in the vents. And it wasn't just him, I also knew the people in the building were signaling each other about me. They do this thing with their coffee cups when I walk by. Coffee cups... you know, I found this mug in the trash once, perfectly good ceramic mug. It had a picture of a lighthouse on it. I always wanted to visit a lighthouse. They have those big spiral staircases inside. Must take forever to walk up all those steps. Imagine carrying a bucket of paint up a spiral staircase. I painted my aunt's house once. It was this awful shade of green, like pea soup. She loved it, though. Made me meatloaf every night I worked on it. Meatloaf with ketchup on top. I don't really like ketchup, it's too sweet. But anyway, yeah, even when I'm feeling calm, the voice is still there, and the signaling with the cups.
Have you ever had a period where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? Yeah... yeah, there are times like that. On my bad days, I just... I sit on the edge of the bed right after my morning prayer, and I just feel so heavy. Empty, you know? Like there's absolutely no point in even cleaning myself up or walking out the front door. I just stare at the floorboards. My floorboards are that cheap laminate stuff, you know the kind? It's supposed to look like oak, but it just looks like plastic. It peels up at the corners if you get it too wet. I tried fixing it once with some superglue, but I ended up getting the glue all over my fingers. Have you ever done that? It takes days to wear off. You feel like you're wearing a second skin. Skin... you know, my grandfather used to have this condition where his skin would flake off like snow. He was a tough old guy, worked in a steel mill his whole life. He had these massive hands. He could probably crush a baseball if he wanted to. I always liked baseball. I used to listen to the games on this little transistor radio I had. It had a silver antenna that you had to pull out, and sometimes you had to wrap tin foil around it just to get a clear signal. But yeah... sitting on the bed, feeling heavy... it happens a lot.
Have the voices and the feeling that people are signaling about you lasted at least one month?

Yeah, oh yeah, it's been way longer than a month. The voices and... and just knowing that they're watching me, marking me with those cups and everything... that's been going on for about a year and a half now. A year and a half. That's a long time. It feels like a long time. You know, a year and a half ago, that's when I bought this new pair of work boots. Steel-toed, real heavy duty. You need steel toes in my line of work, just in case you drop a buffer or something. I dropped a buffer once, not on my foot, thank God, but it took a chunk right out of the baseboard. The building manager was furious. He was this little guy with a mustache that looked like a caterpillar. He used to chew on these wooden matchsticks all day. I don't know why he didn't just chew gum. Gum is so much better for your teeth. My dentist told me that. Dr. Henderson. He had this waiting room with a giant fish tank in it. I used to watch the little neon tetras swim around while I waited. They're so fast, those little fish. Hard to catch, I bet. I went fishing once when I was a kid... but yeah, a year and a half. That's how long the voices have been there.
Have you ever had a period of feeling unusually high or powerful that lasted at least a week?

Yeah, a week or even longer sometimes. I'll get this feeling like... like I'm just buzzing with power, you know? I feel so high up, like nothing can touch me. I'll be laughing and talking real loud to everybody I see, just feeling fantastic. But then, if somebody looks at me wrong or questions what I'm doing, I just snap. I'll start shouting over the tiniest little thing. Like this one time, I was feeling real good, and the guy at the deli counter took too long with my ham. It was just ham, right? Black Forest ham. That's the best kind. It has that dark edge on it. I wonder how they get it so dark. Do they smoke it? My uncle had a smoker in his backyard. He used to make these ribs that would just fall right off the bone. He’d use hickory wood, I think. Hickory is a tough wood. They make baseball bats out of hickory sometimes, or is that ash? Ash trees have been dying off lately because of those little green bugs. Emerald ash borers, they call them. Nasty little things, eating up all the trees. We had a big tree in our front yard when I was growing up, but lightning struck it. Split it right down the middle. Sounded like a bomb went off. But yeah, if I'm feeling that powerful and someone questions me, I just lose it and start shouting.
During the past year and a half, have there been times when the voice and the feeling that people were signaling about you went away completely?

Went away completely? No... no, they never really stop. I mean, there have been calmer weeks, sure. Times when I wasn't feeling all buzzed up and powerful, and I wasn't feeling heavy and depressed either. Just... normal, I guess? But even then, during those calm stretches, for more than two weeks straight I'd still hear the man in the vents. And I still knew the people in the building were signaling about me. 

The vents... you know, the vents in that building are an absolute nightmare to clean. The dust gets caked on those metal slats, thick like dryer lint. Being the janitor, I have to use this special duster on a long telescoping pole just to reach them. I bought it at this little hardware store down on 4th street. The guy who runs the register there, he has a glass eye. You can always tell because it just stays perfectly still while his good eye looks at you. It doesn't track right. Makes you wonder how he lost it, you know? Maybe a woodworking accident? My dad used to do woodworking in the garage. He built this beautiful cedar chest for my mother. Cedar smells so good, doesn't it? It's supposed to keep the moths away. Moths will eat right through a good wool sweater if you aren't careful. I had a sweater once, navy blue, but it got holes all chewed up in the sleeves so I had to throw it out. 

But yeah... even when my mood is completely fine for a couple weeks, the man in the vents is still talking, and the signaling doesn't stop.
During a time when your mood felt completely normal, did the voice and the signaling beliefs continue for at least two weeks?

Yeah, exactly like I was just saying... even when my mood was completely fine, like, not high and buzzed, and not all heavy and depressed either, those things didn't stop. For more than two weeks straight, just feeling normal, I'd still hear that man in the vents clear as day, and I still knew about the signaling. 

It's strange how time works when you're just feeling normal, you know? Like, two weeks can feel like a month, or a month can feel like a few days. I had this watch once, a Timex. It had that Indiglo thing where you push the button and the face lights up blue. I loved that watch. I wore it every day until the strap broke. It was one of those stretchy metal bands, and it kept pinching my arm hair anyway. My arm hair is pretty thick. My grandfather had hairy arms too, like a gorilla, my grandma used to say. She baked the best apple pies. She'd put a little cheddar cheese in the crust. Sounds weird, but it was so good. The salty and the sweet together. Kind of like trail mix. I always pick the M&Ms out of the trail mix first, though. Doesn't everybody? But yeah, even when I was feeling totally normal for more than two weeks, the voice and the signaling were still there.

patient.answer:
Yeah, exactly like I was just saying... even when my mood was completely fine, like, not high and buzzed, and not all heavy and depressed either, those things didn't stop. For more than two weeks straight, just feeling normal, I'd still hear that man in the vents clear as day, and I still knew about the signaling. 

It's strange how time works when you're just feeling normal, you know? Like, two weeks can feel like a month, or a month can feel like a few days. I had this watch once, a Timex. It had that Indiglo thing where you push the button and the face lights up blue. I loved that watch. I wore it every day until the strap broke. It was one of those stretchy metal bands, and it kept pinching my arm hair anyway. My arm hair is pretty thick. My grandfather had hairy arms too, like a gorilla, my grandma used to say. She baked the best apple pies. She'd put a little cheddar cheese in the crust. Sounds weird, but it was so good. The salty and the sweet together. Kind of like trail mix. I always pick the M&Ms out of the trail mix first, though. Doesn't everybody? But yeah, even when I was feeling totally normal for more than two weeks, the voice and the signaling were still there.

inference.note: Psychosis has persisted for >1 year and continues for >2 weeks during euthymic periods, while there are also clear manic episodes and depressive episodes. This rules out mood disorder with psychotic symptoms (F31.2) and schizophrenia subtypes without prominent mood syndrome (F20.0, F20.1), leaving schizoaffective disorder, manic type.

opening_question.intent: Understand the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, persecutory/reference delusions, disorganized/tangential speech) for about 1.5 years, along with clear mood episodes in both manic and depressive directions. Critically, psychotic symptoms continued for more than 2 weeks during periods of euthymic mood, which supports schizoaffective disorder rather than a primary mood disorder with psychotic features. The manic symptoms are prominent, supporting the manic type.
